paragraphs.source_en: The original villa, built when Sahei first felt his company was safely established, was a small structure. Later, however, as the Inugami businesses expanded and Sahei amassed a fortune, he gradually bought up the surrounding land and continued to add to the building, until in the end, it had become a complex maze with numerous annexes. It was so complex, in fact, that had Kindaichi wandered onto the estate alone, he would surely have become lost.

Later, however, as the Inugami businesses expanded and Sahei amassed a fortune, he gradually bought up the surrounding land and continued to add to the building, until in the end, it had become a complex maze with numerous annexes.
It was so complex, in fact, that had Kindaichi wandered onto the estate alone, he would surely have become lost.

paragraphs.source_en: Furudate, however, seemed thoroughly acquainted with the grounds and dragged Kindaichi deeper and deeper without any hesitation. Finally, after passing through a European-style outer garden, they entered the Japanese-style inner garden, where a crowd of policemen, soaked in the rain, milled about searching for something.

paragraphs.source_en: On the other side of a neatly swept carpet of white sand stood a tastefully designed traditional building, probably a teahouse. It was surrounded by rows of chrysanthemums covered by a latticed awning. Large blooms of various types---spherical, cascading, and single-layered---filled the melancholy, rain-drenched garden with their fragrance.

paragraphs.source_en: Pushing the policemen aside, Kindaichi made his way to the front and stood in front of the chrysanthemums. He recalled what Furudate had said once before: "Monkey? He's a master chrysanthemum grower. And now, he's engrossed in making chrysanthemum dolls." Yes, these were Monkey's chrysanthemum dolls alright, and they were arranged to represent a scene from *The Chrysanthemum Garden,* a kabuki play about a legendary hero of medieval Japan.
